T1Distinctiveness.evidence: The rendered library remains recognisably Mez without relying on product colour: authored light/charcoal splits, full-height material rails, Wings geometry, source-labelled runtime twins and the halftone dot portrait remain legible structural devices.

T2Repetition.evidence: The functional library uses distinct composition families for discovery, comparison, checkout, bundle building, horizontal upsell, sticky summary, catalogue matrix, split footer, navigation state system and runtime portrait/marquee twins. ProductFeatureBento was rebuilt from inset mini-cards into four full compositions before scoring.

T3MotionTruth.evidence: No Figma object claims executable motion. Global Navigation, Halftone Portrait and Testimonial Marquee explicitly identify themselves as static state or first-frame twins, preserve reduced/static states, and route live behaviour to the repository contracts. Runtime motion proof is therefore not fabricated in Figma.

T4ProductTruth.evidence: Product components use the five canonical Product Material instances; Wings and identity primitives come from canonical sources; the Halftone twin uses the locked treatment; and the testimonial placeholder was replaced with Kayvon Jafarzadeh's exact approved repository fixture and matching media before scoring.

reviewMethod.compactAndWide: Explicit Wide and Compact runtime variants were rendered and read. Figma does not execute browser viewport reflow, so no browser-width claim is made for this static companion.
reviewMethod.canonSweep: Checked the rendered sets against the Phase B pantry, Product Card ethos, Anti-Slop Canon and Craft composition families; then re-rendered the corrected bento and marquee before scoring.

recommendation.reason: The companion is now a practical, restrained mirror of the repository system: real materials remain the protagonist, functional variants are editable and detachable, and runtime-only behaviour is represented honestly instead of simulated.
